title: Why Small Faith Can Move Big Mountains
paragraphs:
Why Small Faith Can Move Big Mountains
The Day You Stopped Believing in Yourself Might Be the Day God Starts Showing His Power
There is a lie many Christians quietly carry.

It follows them into church.
It sits beside them during prayer.
It whispers to them after every failure.
"If my faith were stronger, God would finally use me."

Waiting until they become spiritually stronger.
Waiting until they stop struggling.
Waiting until they stop doubting.
Waiting until they become the version of themselves they imagine God can finally bless.
And while they wait, mountains remain standing.
But what if the greatest misunderstanding about faith is not how much faith you have...
but what your faith is attached to?
Jesus shattered that misconception with a statement so shocking that many of us have heard it too often to feel its weight anymore.
"For truly I tell you, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you."
The Greek text uses the word πίστις (pistis) for faith.
A mustard seed is almost laughably small.
Jesus could have chosen an oak tree.
He could have chosen a mighty cedar of Lebanon.
Something that could easily be overlooked.
Something many people would dismiss as insignificant.
Because Jesus was never trying to impress people with the size of faith.
He was teaching them about the greatness of the One faith rests upon.
The power was never in the seed.
The power was always in God.
Because most believers secretly measure faith like a spiritual weightlifting competition.
We compare ourselves to biblical heroes.
Then we look at our own lives and see fear.
Yet Scripture repeatedly tells a different story.
And still God worked through them.
One of the most beautiful moments in all of Scripture comes from a desperate father whose son was suffering terribly.
He approached Jesus carrying years of heartbreak.
And when Jesus challenged him to believe, the father cried out:
Not because the man's faith was perfect.
But because it was placed in the perfect Savior.
Somebody reading this understands exactly what that feels like.
You pray but still wrestle with fear.
You trust God while wondering why the answer has not come.
You love Jesus but still battle old wounds.
The enemy wants you to believe your weakness cancels God's ability.
The Apostle Paul learned this firsthand.
After pleading with God repeatedly to remove his thorn in the flesh, the Lord answered:
"My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness." (2 Corinthians 12:9)
Notice what God did not say.
He did not say His power is perfected through human confidence.
He did not say His power is perfected through flawless believers.
He said His power is perfected in weakness.
That means the very thing you are ashamed of may become the stage upon which God's glory is displayed.
This is the pattern of Scripture.
The cross itself became the ultimate picture.
What looked like defeat became victory.
What looked like shame became salvation.
What looked like death became eternal life.
This truth becomes even more powerful when we understand what Jesus meant by mountains.
In biblical language, mountains often represented impossibilities.
The mountain in your life may not be physical.
The mountain may still be standing today.
But your mountain is not greater than your God.
The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly emphasize this truth.
"Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain."
"Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of hosts."
לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם־בְּרוּחִי
(Lo b'chayil v'lo b'koach ki im b'ruchi)
"Not by military force, not by human strength, but by My Spirit."
And maybe that is why your weakness is not the obstacle you think it is.
Maybe God is removing every reason you would trust yourself so that when the mountain finally moves, everyone knows who moved it.
The world tells us to believe in ourselves.
The Gospel tells us to believe in Christ.
The world says strength creates miracles.
The Gospel says surrender creates room for God's power.
Because suddenly faith becomes accessible to the exhausted mother.
The person hanging on by a thread.
If you still have enough faith to whisper the name of Jesus, you have enough faith to come to Him.
If you still have enough faith to pray through tears, you have enough faith to approach Him.
If you still have enough faith to say, "Lord, help me," you have enough faith to experience His grace.
The mountain does not move because your faith is enormous.
The mountain moves because your God is.
And maybe today you needed that reminder.
Not that you need more confidence in yourself.
But that Jesus remains worthy of your trust.
Even when the mountain still stands.
And your story is not finished yet.
Because one shared testimony can reach a soul you will never meet this side of eternity.
